title: trace/v1 event (one JSONL line = one event)
description: One edge in the append-only Decision-Evidence trace ledger. See docs/protocols/trace-v1.md. A ledger is a sequence of these objects, one per line (JSONL); this schema validates a single event object, not the file as a whole. Corrections are new events carrying `supersedes_event_id` -- a conformant writer/reader MUST NOT rewrite or delete a past line.

event_id.description: Deterministic, idempotent identity: "tr1_" + lowercase hex sha256 of the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of {schema: "trace/v1", relation, identity}, where `identity` is the relation-specific field subset defined in docs/protocols/trace-v1.md section 3. A reader MUST recompute this and reject the event if it does not match the declared value.

relation.description: Closed set. `incident_observed` and `rolled_back_to` are reserved for future use (no v1 fixture exercises them, but they are valid values a v1 reader MUST accept, not reject).

occurred_at.description: UTC only. This ledger has no concept of a local-offset timestamp -- every writer MUST convert to UTC and render with a literal "Z" suffix before emitting.

causation_event_id.description: event_id of the event that caused this one (a different relationship than supersedes_event_id, which is about correction, not causation).

payload.description: Relation-specific body. Left unconstrained here (each relation defines its own shape informally in docs/protocols/trace-v1.md); it is deliberately excluded from the event_id identity computation as a whole so an emitter-version bump or additional diagnostic field never changes an event's id. A relation MAY still name specific payload sub-fields as identity inputs (see usage_imported's window.since/window.until in the protocol doc) -- that is a named exception per relation, not a general inclusion of payload.

supersedes_event_id.description: event_id of the event this one corrects. The superseded event is never rewritten or removed -- both rows remain in the ledger permanently. A reader MAY find no event with this id in the segment it has loaded (the original could be in an earlier ledger segment/file it hasn't read); that MUST NOT be treated as a validation failure at the single-event level (see docs/protocols/trace-v1.md section 9).

ref.description: Identifies one endpoint of an edge. An artifact_revision node's logical_id is the bare logical id (e.g. "intent.yaml"); its content_digest pins one specific revision, together forming the <logical_id>@sha256:<digest> two-part node identity described in the platform's Decision-Evidence Graph design. A runtime_entity node (a run, a session, a release, ...) has no content revision, so content_digest is absent and logical_id alone (e.g. "run:<id>", "session:<id>") is the whole identity.
